reason: Conversation 2 ran a sensible, efficient diagnostic path (handheld-only test, light pattern, clean stop vs pulsing), explained the under-load voltage-sag mechanism, and gave the homeowner a direct answer while still flagging that a control fault is the reason not to buy a battery blindly. Conversation 1 made one useful check (charger/contacts) and correctly hedged that the battery is 'most likely' but unconfirmed, yet its final turn was a non-sequitur ('if you can't check it') that ignored the customer's direct question and wrongly pointed to an appliance engineer rather than Dyson support. Neither asked for the model label (SV11) or proposed a known-good-battery swap/Dyson diagnosis before purchase, and Conversation 2 slightly over-rated the floorhead restriction and repeated filter-drying advice already covered, so the margin is clear rather than decisive.
